title: Broiler.Documents corpus round-trip baseline
description: One row per round trip in tests/corpus/corpus.json that loses something or warns about something. Round trips absent from this file are asserted to be lossless and silent, so a new loss fails by not being listed rather than by being listed differently - which keeps the file readable and keeps the check that matters from depending on somebody having written a row for the case that broke. A row that stops reproducing fails too: the point of separating a documented limitation from a suspected defect is to watch the second list shrink, and a shrink nobody records is a shrink nobody can show.

sample.description: The corpus document, generated or authored.

source.description: The format it was read from.

via.description: The format it was written to and read back through.

differences.description: The comparison's own differences, as kind@paragraph: detail. Absolute paths, byte counts and durations are deliberately absent: a baseline carrying a temporary directory would differ on every run, and one carrying a byte count would fail whenever a writer changed something that made no difference to the document.

diagnostics.description: Diagnostic codes, and only codes. Every code except the per-format read summaries, which every package reader emits on every document and which would say only that a read happened. Severity is deliberately not filtered: a codec may report a real skip at info - the RTF reader does when it steps over a picture - and hiding those made a documented, tested, reported behaviour look like a silent loss, which is how one came to be classified as a defect. Messages are excluded because they embed paths and third-party exception text; the code is the stable contract, the message is not.

state.description: documented - a limitation one of the conformance documents states. suspected-defect - a difference nobody decided on, which docs/cli.md says is what round-tripping is actually good for. accepted - the normalized model's own behaviour, looked at and accepted.

reference.description: A repository-relative path to the document that settles the row. Required for a documented row, and CorpusBaselineGuardTests checks that the file is really there - a citation nobody can follow is the same as none.

why.description: What is happening and why it has the state it has. Written for somebody deciding whether a failing run is a regression or a fix.

reviewer.description: Who classified the row. Required unless the state is suspected-defect, which is the state an unreviewed row starts in.

then.description: A row is not classified by being written down. This mirrors PdfTestControlGuardTests.No_Tool_Is_Approved_Merely_By_Being_Written_Down, which makes the same demand of the tool manifest.
